name: Mooren Ulcer

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence reported in African and Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Mooren Ulcer

criteria.description: Presence of painful, progressive, crescent-shaped peripheral corneal ulceration without scleral involvement
Exclusion of systemic autoimmune or infectious diseases causing peripheral ulcerative keratitis
Evidence of stromal inflammation and thinning at the ulcer margin
Severe ocular pain disproportionate to clinical findings
Improvement or stabilization with immunosuppressive therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of peripheral corneal ulceration with stromal inflammation and exclusion of systemic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and by exclusion; biopsy is rarely performed.

searchTerms: peripheral corneal ulcer with crescent shape

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe ocular pain disproportionate to clinical signs
searchTerms: severe eye pain with little visible damage
intense ocular discomfort disproportionate to signs
eye pain worse than expected from exam

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive stromal thinning at ulcer margin
searchTerms: thinning of corneal tissue near ulcer
inflammation of white eye layer near ulcer
scleral redness adjacent to corneal sore

rare.symptomName: Corneal scarring leading to permanent vision loss
searchTerms: permanent vision impairment from corneal damage
scar tissue on cornea affecting sight

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) may be present but nonspecific
Negative autoimmune serologies (e.g., ANCA, rheumatoid factor) to exclude systemic vasculitis
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing peripheral corneal ulceration with undermined edges
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating stromal thinning
other: Histopathology (rarely performed) shows stromal infiltration by inflammatory cells without vasculitis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic autoimmune disease (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis)
Presence of infectious agents (bacterial, fungal, viral)

redFlags: Rapid progression of corneal ulceration despite treatment
Severe vision loss or sudden decrease in visual acuity
references: Dua HS, et al. Mooren's ulcer: a review. Surv Ophthalmol. 2000;44(3):207-17.
Liu Z, et al. Clinical features and treatment of Mooren ulcer: a retrospective study. BMC Ophthalmol. 2018;18(1):1-8.
